evals.prompt: Evaluate my Flutter project. It is a standard single-app project with lib/, android/ and ios/ folders. I want to know whether it complies with Pragma best practices.
evals.expected_output: The agent detects that it is a single-app project, evaluates the repository across the 5 domains (Maintainability, Traceability, Performance, Security, Documentation) by loading each reference file, and generates reports/flutter_rules_report.md with a ✔️/❌/⚠️/N/A table, executive summary and suggested steps.
expectations: The agent correctly detects that it is a single-app project before evaluating
The agent loads at least one references/ file (maintainability.md, traceability.md, performance.md, security.md or documentation.md) during the evaluation
The report is generated at reports/flutter_rules_report.md
The report contains an Executive Summary table with counts for ✔️, ❌, ⚠️ and N/A
The report has separate sections for the 5 domains with criteria tables
The report includes a Suggested Steps section with at least one concrete action

evals.prompt: I have a Flutter monorepo with folders apps/app_client, apps/app_admin, and packages/shared_auth. Does it comply with Pragma rules? Evaluate everything.
evals.expected_output: The agent detects the monorepo, reads references/monorepo.md for evaluation logic, classifies the projects (2 apps + 1 package), evaluates each one with the correct path scope, verifies shared_auth cross-impact on both apps, and produces reports/flutter_rules_report.md with a consolidated summary, cross-impact table, and sections per project.
expectations: The agent reads references/monorepo.md to obtain the monorepo evaluation algorithm
The agent classifies app_client and app_admin as App projects, and shared_auth as a Package
The agent uses different paths: apps/app_client/lib/ for app_client, packages/shared_auth/lib/ for shared_auth
The report has a Consolidated Summary section with a table of projects and their debt level
The report has a Cross-Impact Findings section when it finds problems in shared_auth
Android/iOS criteria are marked as N/A in the shared_auth section
The report is generated at reports/flutter_rules_report.md

evals.prompt: I only want to review the Security domain of my Flutter app. We have a release tomorrow and the security team asked me for a quick checklist.
evals.expected_output: The agent understands that only the Security domain is requested, loads only references/security.md, evaluates the project against that domain, and generates a partial report with only the Security section without evaluating the other 4 domains.
expectations: The agent loads references/security.md to obtain Security domain rules
The agent evaluates http:// usage without TLS, print( in production, and possible hardcoded credentials
The report contains the Security section with a criteria table
The report is generated at reports/flutter_rules_report.md
The agent does NOT evaluate unrequested domains (Maintainability, Traceability, Performance, Documentation) or marks them as out of scope

evals.prompt: Evaluate my Flutter monorepo with Melos. The structure is: melos.yaml at the root, apps/mobile_app/, features/auth_feature/, features/checkout_feature/, and shared/design_system/. I want to know the overall status and which packages have the most technical debt.
evals.expected_output: The agent detects melos.yaml, reads references/monorepo.md, classifies the projects (1 app + 2 features + 1 shared), uses melos.yaml as the source of truth for the package list, evaluates each one with the correct scope (features and shared without Android/iOS criteria), reports shared/design_system cross-impact on the features and app, and produces a consolidated summary showing the project with the highest debt.
expectations: The agent detects melos.yaml and uses it as the source of truth to list workspace projects
The agent reads references/monorepo.md to obtain classification and scoping logic
mobile_app is evaluated with App criteria including Android/iOS; features and shared have native platform criteria marked as N/A
The agent verifies which features and apps consume shared/design_system by reading each project pubspec.yaml
The report includes a Consolidated Summary table showing all projects and their debt level
The report identifies the project with the highest technical debt in the Consolidated Summary
The Cross-Impact Findings section shows which projects are affected by problems in shared/design_system
